I am an old man of 72 years, and I have been farming these lands in the North West for many seasons. On this small plot of one quarter hectare, I plant my beans together with some millet or sorghum as my fathers did. I have small money, so I will use a little fertilizer because the soil here is tired, but beans do not need much nitrogen — they make their own from the air. My own seed from last harvest is good enough, and my sons and grandchildren will help me with the work since my back is no longer strong.
